ideas.name: RightsFlow
ideas.problem: Creators lose significant revenue through unmonitored license expirations, allowing brands to use content for free beyond agreed terms while missing proactive opportunities to pitch contract extensions.
ideas.targetUser: Freelance UGC creators and micro-influencers (primarily Gen Z/Millennial) managing 5+ active brand deals who lack legal teams and struggle with manual contract tracking.
coreFeatures: Contract Vault: A centralized repository for storing contract PDFs and extracting key terms (usage duration, platform limits, and territory).
Expiration Countdown Dashboard: A visual timeline/calendar view showing exactly how many days of usage remain for every active deal.
Auto-Pitch Engine: One-click generation of personalized renewal emails/DMs based on the specific brand and contract terms.
Compliance Alert System: High-priority notifications that trigger when a brand is using content outside of its legal window (Usage Overages).
realDependencies: Gmail/Outlook API for automated outreach
OpenAI API for parsing contract text into structured data
Google Drive/Dropbox API for secure document storage
Stripe API for managing renewal payments/invoicing
ideas.emulationStrategy: The demo will use a local JSON manifest to simulate a database of 'Active Deals' with varying expiration dates. To mimic the AI contract parser, the app will use a regex-based string extractor that 'finds' dates in a text block to simulate LLM intelligence. API calls for 'Sending Pitch' will be intercepted by a service layer that introduces a 2-second artificial delay followed by a successful JSON response. A scheduled 'Time-Skip' button will be implemented to fast-forward the app's internal clock, triggering the 'Compliance Alert' and 'Renewal Due' UI states to demonstrate the notification logic.

ideas.name: CueCheck
ideas.problem: Wasted production time and diminished recording quality caused by unexpected guest technical failures (poor mic levels, unstable internet, or bad lighting) discovered only after the session has started.
ideas.targetUser: Professional podcast producers, remote-first studio managers, and high-profile thought leaders who conduct remote interviews and require a polished, 'zero-troubleshooting' guest experience.
coreFeatures: One-Click Hardware Audit (Mic sensitivity, sample rate, and headset detection)
Network Jitter & Bandwidth Stress Test (Simulated packet loss and upload speed verification)
AI-Driven Lighting & Framing Analysis (Webcam-based assessment of brightness and background clutter)
Instant Host Readiness Score (A shareable, real-time dashboard for the host to see guest status)
realDependencies: Web Audio API (for decibel and frequency analysis)
WebRTC (for real-time media stream testing)
TensorFlow.js (for computer vision lighting/framing detection)
Network Information API (for bandwidth/connection metrics)
Firebase Realtime Database (for syncing guest scores to host dashboards)
ideas.emulationStrategy: The demo will use a 'Mock Diagnostic Engine' that replaces real hardware calls. Audio levels will be simulated using a looping sine wave with randomized amplitude to mimic 'unstable' mic levels. Network tests will use a pseudo-random delay generator (setTimeout with Math.random() * 1500ms) to simulate latency and jitter. The lighting analysis will bypass TensorFlow.js by providing a 'Scenario Selector' (e.g., 'Dark Room', 'Bright Office') that returns hardcoded JSON lighting values. All 'uploading score' actions will be intercepted by an async function that mimics a 2-second network delay before returning a 200 OK response with a dummy Readiness Score.

ideas.name: LoreLogic
ideas.niche: Non-linear narrative state management and logic auditing for interactive fiction
ideas.problem: The 'Continuity Drift' problem where complex branching paths lead to logical contradictions, such as characters possessing items they shouldn't or referencing plot events that were bypassed, which are nearly impossible to track manually in spreadsheets.
ideas.targetUser: Professional Narrative Designers, Indie Game Writers, and Technical Storytellers working on RPGs, Visual Novels, and choice-driven adventure titles.
coreFeatures: Visual Logic Flowchart: A node-based interface to map branching decisions and their resulting state changes visually.
Continuity Conflict Engine: An automated auditor that scans paths to identify logical contradictions in character states or inventory ownership.
Global Variable Registry: A centralized dashboard for managing all booleans, integers, and string variables used across the entire script.
Script Schema Importer: A tool to ingest .ink or .json files to auto-generate the logic graph and variable list.
realDependencies: WebAssembly-based script parsers (for Ink/Twine support)
Graph visualization libraries (e.g., React Flow or Cytoscape.js)
Cloud database for project versioning and collaboration (e.g., PostgreSQL or Supabase)
File System Access API for local workspace integration
ideas.emulationStrategy: The demo will use a static 'Project Manifest' JSON to simulate a loaded game script. The Continuity Conflict Engine will trigger a 2.5-second simulated 'scanning' animation before returning a pre-defined set of 'logic errors' (e.g., 'Error: Variable [is_dead] is TRUE, but Dialogue Node [B] is reachable') mapped to specific node IDs in the manifest. Cloud synchronization will be emulated by a service wrapper that adds a 1-second delay to all 'save' actions and occasionally triggers a mock 'Network Timeout' toast to demonstrate error-handling UI.

ideas.name: HookLab
ideas.niche: Short-form video retention optimization and pattern management
ideas.problem: Creators lack a systematic method to catalog, test, and replicate specific visual and auditory patterns that prevent audience drop-off during the first 3 seconds of video.
ideas.targetUser: Intermediate to professional short-form creators and social media agency managers (ages 18-35) who need to scale content production while maintaining high view-duration metrics.
coreFeatures: Pattern Library: A searchable database of categorized visual, auditory, and text-based hooks
Retention Storyboarder: A drag-and-drop tool to map out video pacing and energy curves
Hook A/B Testing Lab: A workspace to track and compare retention metrics for different hook variations
AI Pattern Scout: A tool that identifies recurring visual motifs in trending videos within a specific niche
realDependencies: TikTok/Instagram/YouTube Shorts APIs for real-time performance metrics
OpenAI API for automated pattern description and hook generation
AWS S3 for video snippet and asset storage
PostgreSQL for structured storage of user-generated pattern data
ideas.emulationStrategy: The demo will utilize a mock API layer that serves hardcoded JSON objects representing trending patterns and user metrics. All 'network' requests will be intercepted to include a randomized 800ms-1500ms delay to simulate server latency. The AI pattern analysis will be simulated via a keyword-to-response mapping engine. Data persistence will be achieved through browser localStorage to give the illusion of a live database.

ideas.name: StemLedger
ideas.niche: Music production legal compliance and sample provenance tracking
ideas.problem: The high risk of copyright infringement and lost royalties caused by producers' inability to track the licensing status, origin, and usage permissions of multiple layered samples within complex DAW projects.
ideas.targetUser: Independent and professional music producers, beatmakers, and studio engineers (ages 18-45) working in sample-heavy genres like Hip-Hop, EDM, and Lo-fi who collaborate across remote environments.
coreFeatures: Sample Asset Registry with detailed metadata tagging (Source, BPM, Key, License Type)
Visual Clearance Dashboard using a Traffic-Light system (Green: Cleared, Yellow: Pending, Red: Uncleared)
Automated Provenance Report Generator for distributors and labels
Collaborator Audit Log to track sample additions and status changes within a team
realDependencies: Discogs API for automatic music metadata enrichment
AWS S3 for secure storage of audio snippets and proof of license
DocuSign API for executing digital clearance agreements
ACRCloud API for audio fingerprinting and sample identification
ideas.emulationStrategy: The demo will utilize a local 'mockDatabase.json' containing a curated list of 50 sample entries with pre-set clearance statuses. All API calls will be routed through a 'MockProvider' that uses async/await with a simulated 1200ms latency to mimic network requests. The 'Audio Fingerprinting' feature will be simulated by a 3-second progress bar animation that, upon completion, returns a hardcoded 'Match Found' result from the mock database. Document generation will be emulated by triggering a download of a static, pre-designed PDF file instead of a dynamic build.
